title: SNMPv3 traps should be configured
description: SNMP v3 can be used for remote logging, and is the recommended protocol in higher security situations as it fully supports encryption of logs. PASS requires an SNMP trap server profile using version v3 and System log forwarding to it; also confirm the other log types. Audited against the PAN-OS running configuration in set format: run 'set cli config-output-format set', then 'configure' and 'show' (or 'show config running') and save the full output.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 1.1.1.2 SNMPv3 traps should be configured

remediation.command:
configure
set shared log-settings snmptrap SNMPV3-PROFILE version v3 server NMS1 manager 10.0.0.60 user snmptrapuser engineid 0x80001f888056
set shared log-settings system match-list ALL-SYSTEM filter "All Logs" send-snmptrap SNMPV3-PROFILE
commit
# CIS guidance:
Navigate to Device > Server Profiles > SNMP Trap Choose Add Assign a Name to the Profile, and specify version V3. Choose Add, and assign a server name in the Name field, add an IP address or FQDN in the SNMP Manager field. Edit the Password fields as appropriate for your server. Repeat if multiple Syslog destinations are required.
Navigate to Device > Log Settings Under System, add an entry. Define a Name and a Filter setting. Under Forward Methods, add a SNMP Profile in the SNMP section. Ensure that at least one of the Log Settings Configuration entries has its Filter setting at All Logs Under Configuration, add an entry. Define a Name and a Filter setting. Under Forward Methods, add a SNMP Profile in the SNMP section. Ensure that at least one of the Log Settings Configuration entries has its Filter setting at All Logs Under User-ID, add an entry. Define a Name and a Filter setting. Under Forward Methods, add a SNMP Profile in the SNMP section. Ensure that at least one of the Log Settings Configuration entries has its Filter setting at All Logs Under HIP Match (Host Information Profile), add an entry. Define a Name and a Filter setting. Under Forward Methods, add a SNMP Profile in the SNMP section. Ensure that at least one of the Log Settings Configuration entries has its Filter setting at All Logs Under IP-Tag, add an entry. Define a Name and a Filter setting. Under Forward Methods, add a SNMP Profile in the SNMP section. Ensure that at least one of the Log Settings Configuration entries has its Filter setting at All Logs

reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 1.2.1 Ensure 'Permitted IP Addresses' is set to those necessary for device management

configure
set deviceconfig system permitted-ip 10.0.0.0/24

title: Ensure 'Minimum Password Complexity' is enabled
description: This checks all new passwords to ensure that they meet basic requirements for strong passwords. PASS requires mgt-config password-complexity enabled yes (also set block-username-inclusion yes). Audited against the PAN-OS running configuration in set format: run 'set cli config-output-format set', then 'configure' and 'show' (or 'show config running') and save the full output.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 1.3.1 Ensure 'Minimum Password Complexity' is enabled

remediation.command:
configure
set mgt-config password-complexity enabled yes
set mgt-config password-complexity block-username-inclusion yes
commit
# CIS guidance:
Navigate to Device > Setup > Management > Minimum Password Complexity. Set Enabled to be checked Set that the various password settings to values that are appropriate to your organization. It is suggested that there at least be some special characters enforced, and that a minimum length be set. Ensure that non-zero values are set for Minimum Uppercase, Lowercase and Special Characters. "Block Username Inclusion" should be enabled. Operationally, dictionary words should be avoided for all passwords - passphrases are a much better alternative.

title: Ensure 'Required Password Change Period' is less than or equal to 90 days
description: This defines how long a user can use a password before it expires. PASS requires password-change expiration-period between 1 and 90 days. Audited against the PAN-OS running configuration in set format: run 'set cli config-output-format set', then 'configure' and 'show' (or 'show config running') and save the full output.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 1.3.7 Ensure 'Required Password Change Period' is less than or equal to 90 days

configure
set mgt-config password-complexity password-change expiration-period 90

title: Ensure 'Failed Attempts' and 'Lockout Time' for Authentication Profile are properly configured
description: Configure values for Failed Login Attempts and Account Lockout Time set to organization-defined values (for example, 3 failed attempts and a 15 minute lockout time). Do not set Failed Attempts and Lockout Time in the Authentication Settings section; any Failed Attempts or Lockout Time settings within the selected Authentication Profile do not apply in the Authentication Settings section. PASS requires an authentication profile with non-zero lockout failed-attempts and lockout-time; confirm every profile in use has them. Audited against the PAN-OS running configuration in set format: run 'set cli config-output-format set', then 'configure' and 'show' (or 'show config running') and save the full output.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 1.4.2 Ensure 'Failed Attempts' and 'Lockout Time' for Authentication Profile are properly configured

remediation.command:
configure
set shared authentication-profile <profile> lockout failed-attempts 5
set shared authentication-profile <profile> lockout lockout-time 30
commit
# CIS guidance:
Navigate to Device > Authentication Profile. Set Failed Attempts to the non-zero organization-defined value. Set Lockout Time to the non-zero organization-defined value.

description: This setting determines whether or not the identity of the update server must be verified before performing an update session. Note that if an SSL Forward Proxy is configured to intercept the update session, this option may need to be disabled (because the SSL Certificate will not match). PASS requires deviceconfig system server-verification yes. Audited against the PAN-OS running configuration in set format: run 'set cli config-output-format set', then 'configure' and 'show' (or 'show config running') and save the full output.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 1.6.1 Ensure 'Verify Update Server Identity' is enabled

title: Ensure that WildFire file size upload limits are maximized
description: The default file size limits on the firewall are designed to include the majority of malware in the wild (which is smaller than the default size limits) and to exclude large files that are very unlikely to be malicious and that can impact WildFire file-forwarding capacity.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 5.1 Ensure that WildFire file size upload limits are maximized

audit.command: Device > Setup > WildFire > General Settings: confirm every file-type size limit is at least the default (pe 16MB, apk 10MB, pdf 3072KB, ms-office 16384KB, jar 5MB, flash 5MB, MacOSX 10MB, archive 50MB, linux 50MB, script 20KB) and ideally near the maximum (pe/apk/MacOSX 50MB, pdf/ms-office 51200KB, jar 20MB, flash 10MB, script 4096KB). CLI: show deviceconfig setting wildfire file-size-limit.

remediation.command:
configure
set deviceconfig setting wildfire file-size-limit pe size-limit 50
set deviceconfig setting wildfire file-size-limit pdf size-limit 51200
set deviceconfig setting wildfire file-size-limit ms-office size-limit 51200
commit
# CIS guidance:
Navigate to Device > Setup > WildFire. Click the General Settings edit icon. Set the maximum size for each file type are larger than the defaults, to a size that is as large enough to account for "large" files, but not large enough to affect performance of the hardware. In PAN-OS 9.x and higher, the default file sizes for WildFire are:
pe (Portable Executable) - 16MB apk (Android Application)- 10MB pdf (Portable Document Format) - 3072KB ms-office (Microsoft Office) — 16384KB jar (Packaged Java class file) — 5MB flash (Adobe Flash) — 5MB MacOSX (DMG/MAC-APP/MACH-O PKG files) — 10MB archive (RAR and 7z files) — 50MB linux (ELF files) — 50MB script (JScript, VBScript, PowerShell, and Shell Script)- 20KB In PAN-OS 9.x and higher, the maximum file sizes for Wildfire are:
pe (Portable Executable) - 50MB apk (Android Application)- 50MB pdf (Portable Document Format) - 51200KB ms-office (Microsoft Office) — 51200KB jar (Packaged Java class file) — 20MB flash (Adobe Flash) — 10MB MacOSX (DMG/MAC-APP/MACH-O PKG files) — 50MB archive (RAR and 7z files) — 50MB linux (ELF files) — 50MB script (JScript, VBScript, PowerShell, and Shell Script)- 4096KB

title: Ensure a WildFire Analysis profile is enabled for all security policies
description: Ensure that all files traversing the firewall are inspected by WildFire by setting a Wildfire file blocking profile on all security policies.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 5.2 Ensure a WildFire Analysis profile is enabled for all security policies

audit.command: Objects > Security Profiles > WildFire Analysis: verify a profile exists (Application any, File Types any, Direction both). For each Security rule with action Allow, Actions > Profile Setting must set a WildFire Analysis profile, or a Security Profile Group that includes one.

reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 5.3 Ensure forwarding of decrypted content to WildFire is enabled

reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 5.4 Ensure all WildFire session information settings are enabled

# CIS guidance:
Navigate to Device > Setup > WildFire > Session Information Settings. Set every option to be enabled.

title: Ensure alerts are enabled for malicious files detected by WildFire
description: Configure WildFire to send an alert when a malicious or greyware file is detected. This alert could be sent by whichever means is preferable, including email, SNMP trap, or syslog message. Alternatively, configure the WildFire cloud to generate alerts for malicious files. The cloud can generate alerts in addition to or instead of the local WildFire implementation. Note that the destination email address of alerts configured in the WildFire cloud portal is tied to the logged in account, and cannot be modified. Also, new systems added to the WildFire cloud portal will not be automatically set to email alerts. PASS requires a log forwarding profile with a wildfire log-type match list (filter '(verdict neq benign)' with an alert destination). Audited against the PAN-OS running configuration in set format: run 'set cli config-output-format set', then 'configure' and 'show' (or 'show config running') and save the full output.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 5.5 Ensure alerts are enabled for malicious files detected by WildFire

remediation.command:
configure
set shared log-settings profiles WF-ALERTS match-list malicious log-type wildfire
set shared log-settings profiles WF-ALERTS match-list malicious filter "(verdict neq benign)"
set shared log-settings profiles WF-ALERTS match-list malicious send-syslog SYSLOG-PROFILE
commit
# CIS guidance:
From GUI, configure some combination of the following Server Profiles:
Configure the Email Server: Select Device > Server Profiles > Email Click Add Enter a name for the Profile. Select the virtual system from the Location drop down menu (if applicable) Click Add Configure the Syslog Server: Select Device > Server Profiles > Syslog > Add Enter Name, Display Name, Syslog Server, Transport, Port, Format, Facility Click OK Click Commit to save the configuration Configure the SMTP Server: Select Device > Server Profiles > Email Select Add, Name, Display Name, From, To, Additional Recipients, Gateway IP or Hostname Click OK Click Commit to save the configuration
Navigate to Objects, Log Forwarding Choose Add, set the log type to "wildfire", add the filter "(verdict neq benign)", then add log destinations for SNMP, Syslog, Email or HTTP as required.

title: Choosing Wildfire public cloud region
description: By default, all relevant files are uploaded to Wildfire datacenter located in US. Palo Alto Networks has been adding more WildFire regional clouds around the world. From having just 3 regional clouds back in PanOS 8.x, now to more than 10 regional clouds all over the world.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 5.7 Choosing Wildfire public cloud region

audit.command: Navigate to Device > Setup > WildFire. Navigate to the General Settings sections. Verify that WildFire Public Cloud is set to your appropriate region.

remediation.command:
Navigate to Device > Setup > WildFire.
Navigate to the General Settings sections. Click the General Settings edit icon. Change the WildFire Public Cloud to your appropriate region.

title: Ensure that 'Inline Cloud Analysis' on Wildfire profiles is enabled
description: Enable 'Advanced WildFire Inline Cloud Analysis' on Wildfire profiles and forward PE files for analysis. Palo Alto Networks Advanced WildFire operates a series of cloud- based ML detection engines that provide inline analysis of PE (portable executable) files traversing your network to detect and prevent advanced malware in real-time.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 5.8 Ensure that 'Inline Cloud Analysis' on Wildfire profiles is enabled

audit.command: Navigate to Objects > Security Profiles > Wildfire Verify that Wildfire profiles has Enable cloud inline analysis checked. On Inline cloud analysis tab, verify that there is a rule to forward files with the following settings: Application set to Any File Type set to PE Direction set to Both Action set to Block

remediation.command:
Navigate to Objects > Security Profiles > Wildfire On relevant Wildfire profile, checked Enable cloud inline analysis box. On Inline cloud analysis tab, configure a rule to forward files with the following settings:
Application set to Any File Type set to PE Direction set to Both Action set to Block

title: Ensure that antivirus profiles are set to reset-both on all decoders except 'imap' and 'pop3'
description: Configure antivirus profiles to a value of 'reset-both' for all decoders except imap and pop3 under both Action and WildFire Action. If required by the organization's email implementation, configure imap and pop3 decoders to 'alert' under both Action and WildFire Action. FAILs if any antivirus profile sets action or wildfire-action on the ftp, http, http2, smb or smtp decoder to anything other than reset-both (imap/pop3 may use alert). Audited against the PAN-OS running configuration in set format: run 'set cli config-output-format set', then 'configure' and 'show' (or 'show config running') and save the full output.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 6.1 Ensure that antivirus profiles are set to reset-both on all decoders except 'imap' and 'pop3'

configure
set profiles virus <profile> decoder http action reset-both
set profiles virus <profile> decoder http wildfire-action reset-both
(repeat for ftp, http2, smb, smtp)

# CIS guidance:
Navigate to Objects > Security Profiles > Antivirus. Set antivirus profiles to have all decoders set to reset-both for both Action and Wildfire Action. If imap and pop3 are required in the organization, set the imap and pop3 decoders to alert for both Action and Wildfire Action.

title: Ensure a secure antivirus profile is applied to all relevant security policies
description: Create a secure antivirus profile and apply it to all security policies that could pass HTTP, SMTP, IMAP, POP3, FTP, or SMB traffic. The antivirus profile may be applied to the security policies directly or through a profile group.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 6.2 Ensure a secure antivirus profile is applied to all relevant security policies

audit.command: Navigate to Policies > Security . For each policy, navigate to [Policy Name] > Actions Verify there is a secure Antivirus profile applied to all security policies passing traffic - regardless of protocol. This can be set by Profiles or by Profile Group.

remediation.command: Navigate to Policies > Security . For each policy, navigate to [Policy Name] > Actions Set an Antivirus profile or a Profile Group containing an AV profile for each security policy passing traffic - regardless of protocol.

title: Ensure an anti-spyware profile is configured to block on specified spyware severity levels, categories, and threats
description: If a single rule exists within the anti-spyware profile, configure it to block on Critical, High, and Medium spyware severity level, any category, and any threat. If multiple rules exist within the anti-spyware profile, ensure all spyware categories, threats, and severity levels (Critical, High, and Medium) are set to be blocked. Additional rules may exist for packet capture or exclusion purposes. PASS requires an anti-spyware profile rule with action reset-both; confirm it covers severity critical, high and medium, category any and threat-name any. Audited against the PAN-OS running configuration in set format: run 'set cli config-output-format set', then 'configure' and 'show' (or 'show config running') and save the full output.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 6.3 Ensure an anti-spyware profile is configured to block on specified spyware severity levels, categories, and threats

remediation.command:
configure
set profiles spyware <profile> rules block-crit-high-med severity [ critical high medium ]
set profiles spyware <profile> rules block-crit-high-med category any
set profiles spyware <profile> rules block-crit-high-med threat-name any
set profiles spyware <profile> rules block-crit-high-med action reset-both
commit
# CIS guidance:
Navigate to Objects > Security Profiles > Anti-Spyware. Click on existing profile in used or create a new profile.
Navigate to Signature Policies tab. Add new policy by giving it a name Policy Name. Set a Policy Name exists within the anti-spyware profile that is configured to perform the reset-both on Critical, High, and Medium Severity level, any Category, and any Threat Name.

title: Ensure DNS sinkholing is configured on all anti-spyware profiles in use
description: Configure DNS sinkholing for all anti-spyware profiles in use. All internal requests to the selected sinkhole IP address must traverse the firewall. Any device attempting to communicate with the DNS sinkhole IP address should be considered infected. PASS requires default-paloalto-dns with action sinkhole in an anti-spyware profile; confirm every profile in use and the sinkhole IPv4/IPv6 addresses. Audited against the PAN-OS running configuration in set format: run 'set cli config-output-format set', then 'configure' and 'show' (or 'show config running') and save the full output.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 6.4 Ensure DNS sinkholing is configured on all anti-spyware profiles in use

audit.pattern: (?m)^set (?:shared |vsys \S+ |device-group \S+ |template \S+ config (?:shared |vsys \S+ )?)?profiles spyware (?:"[^"\n]*"|\S+) botnet-domains lists default-paloalto-dns action sinkhole[ \t]*$

remediation.command:
configure
set profiles spyware <profile> botnet-domains lists default-paloalto-dns action sinkhole
set profiles spyware <profile> botnet-domains sinkhole ipv4-address sinkhole.paloaltonetworks.com
set profiles spyware <profile> botnet-domains sinkhole ipv6-address ::1
commit
# CIS guidance:

# CIS guidance:
Navigate to Policies > Decryption. Create a Policy for all traffic destined to the Internet. This Policy should include:
Source tab: The Source Zone and/or Source Address should include all target internal networks. Source User should include all target internal users Destination tab: The Destination Zone should include the untrusted target zone (usually the internet). Destination Address is typically Any for an internet destination. Service/URL Category tab: all URL Category entries should be included except financial-services, government and health-and-medicine (this list may vary depending on your organization and its policies). Options tab: Type set to SSL Forward Proxy

audit.command: Navigate to Policies > Decryption. Verify SSL Inbound Inspection is set appropriately for all untrusted traffic destined for servers using SSL or TLS. Navigate to Policies > Decryption. For each service published to the internet (or other untrusted zones), verify the following settings: General tab: Name set to a descriptive name Source: Source Zone set to the target zone (Internet in many cases). Source Address set to the target address space (Any for internet traffic) Destination tab: Destination Zone should be set to the appropriate zone, or Any. (Full steps: CIS 8.2.)

remediation.command:
Navigate to Policies > Decryption. Set SSL Inbound Inspection appropriately for all untrusted traffic destined for servers using SSL or TLS.
Navigate to Policies > Decryption. For each service published to the internet (or other untrusted zones), create a Policy and set the following options:
General tab: Name set to a descriptive name Source: Source Zone set to the target zone (Internet in many cases). title: Ensure that the Certificate used for Decryption is Trusted
description: The CA Certificate used for in-line HTTP Man in the Middle should be trusted by target users. For SSL Forward Proxy configurations, there are classes of users that need to be considered. 1: Users that are members of the organization, users of machines under control of the organization. For these people and machines, ensure that the CA Certificate is in one of the Trusted CA certificate stores. This is easily done in Active Directory, using Group Policies for instance. A MDM (Mobile Device Manager) can be used to accomplish the same task for mobile devices such as telephones or tablets.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 8.3 Ensure that the Certificate used for Decryption is Trusted

audit.command: Verify the CA Certificate(s): Navigate to Device > Certificate Management > Certificates Verify that appropriate internal certificates are imported, and that all certificates in the list are valid. In particular, verify the Subject, Issuer, CA, Expires, Algorithm and Usage fields Alternatively, if an internal CA is implemented on the firewall, verify that target clients have the root certificate for this CA imported into their list of trusted certificate authorities. (Full steps: CIS 8.3.)

remediation.command:

Alternatively, generate a self-signed certificate for an internal CA on the firewall, and then import the root certificate for that CA into the trusted CA list of target clients. In an Active Directory environment this can be facilitated using a Group Policy. Set the Certificate Profile needed for the SSL Forward Proxy:
Navigate to Device > Certificate Management > Certificate Profile. Set the decryption profile to include the settings described in the SSL Forward Proxy guidance in this document

title: Ensure that the Certificate Securing Remote Access VPNs is Valid
description: The Certificate used to secure Remote Access VPNs should satisfy the following criteria: It should be a valid certificate from a trusted source. In almost cases this means a trusted Public Certificate Authority, as in most cases remote access VPN users will not have access to any Private Certificate Authorities for Certificate validation. The certificate should have a valid date. It should not have a "to" date in the past (it should not be expired), and should not have a "from" date in the future. The key length used to encrypt the certificate should be 2048 bits or more. The hash used to sign the certificate should be SHA-2 or better.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 1.6.3 Ensure that the Certificate Securing Remote Access VPNs is Valid

audit.command: Verify that the certificate being used to secure the VPN meets the criteria listed above: Navigate to Device > Certificate Management > Certificates Ensure that a valid certificate is applied to the HTTPS portal: Navigate to Network > GlobalProtect > Portals > Portal Configuration > (Select the Portal being assessed) > Authentication > SSL/TLS Profile Ensure that a valid certificate is applied to the GlobalProtect Gateway: Navigate to Network > GlobalProtect > Gateways > (Select the Gateway being Assessed) > Authentication > SSL/TLS Service Profile Ensure that ... (Full steps: CIS 1.6.3.)

remediation.command:
Create a CSR and install a certificate from a public CA (Certificate Authority) here:
Navigate to Device > Certificate Management > Certificates Apply a valid certificate to the HTTPS portal:
Navigate to Network > GlobalProtect > Portals > Portal Configuration > Authentication > SSL/TLS Profile Apply a valid certificate to the GlobalProtect Gateway:
Navigate to Network > GlobalProtect > Gateways > Authentication > SSL/TLS Service Profile Configure the Service Profile to use the correct certificate Ensure that the Minimum TLS version is set to 1.1 or 1.2 (1.2 is recommended).

title: Enabling Post-Quantum (PQ) on IKEv2 VPNs
description: For VPN that has IKEv2 enabled, enable PQ for more secure way to exchange pre- shared secret to defend against "Harvest Now, Decrypt Later" attack technique.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 1.7.1 Enabling Post-Quantum (PQ) on IKEv2 VPNs

audit.command: Navigate to Network > Network Profiles > IKE Gateways. On gateways that has IKEv2 enabled, click into it and navigate to Advanced Options. On IKEv2 section, navigate to PQ PPK section. Verify that Enable Post-Quantum Pre-Shared Key (PPK) is checked. Negotiation mode should be set to Mandatory if both sides of VPN supports PQ. Negotiation mode should be set to Preferred if you don't know or don't have control over whether the peer supports RFC 8784. Preferred mode preserves backward compatibility to ensure connections fall back instead of dropping. (Full steps: CIS 1.7.1.)

remediation.command: Navigate to Network > Network Profiles > IKE Gateways. On gateways that has IKEv2 enabled, click into it and navigate to Advanced Options. On IKEv2 section, navigate to PQ PPK section. Check Enable Post-Quantum Pre-Shared Key (PPK) option. Negotiation mode should be set to Mandatory if both sides of VPN supports PQ. Negotiation mode should be set to Preferred if you don't know or don't have control over whether the peer supports RFC 8784. Preferred mode preserves backward compatibility to ensure connections fall back instead of dropping. If both sides of VPN supports more than 1 PPK key ID, then multiple PPK key ID should be configured. Configuring multiple PQ PPKs is most secure because it adds a random element to PQ PPK selection.

title: Ensure that IP addresses are mapped to usernames
description: Configure appropriate settings to map IP addresses to usernames. Mapping userids to IP addresses is what permits the firewall to create rules based on userids and groups rather than IP addresses and subnets, as well as log events by userids rather than IP addresses or DNS names. The specifics of how to achieve IP-to-username mapping is highly dependent on the environment. It can be enabled by integrating the firewall with a domain controller, Exchange server, captive portal, Terminal Server, User-ID Agent, XML API, or syslog data from a variety of devices. PASS requires at least one zone with enable-user-identification yes (the PDF also checks that trusted-zone traffic logs show Source User). Audited against the PAN-OS running configuration in set format: run 'set cli config-output-format set', then 'configure' and 'show' (or 'show config running') and save the full output.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 2.1 Ensure that IP addresses are mapped to usernames

remediation.command:
configure
set zone <trusted-zone> enable-user-identification yes

description: Only enable the User-ID option for interfaces that are both internal and trusted. There is rarely a legitimate need to allow WMI probing (or any user-id identification) on an untrusted interface. The exception to this is identification of remote-access VPN users, who are identified as they connect.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 2.3 Ensure that User-ID is only enabled for internal trusted interfaces

title: Ensure that 'Include/Exclude Networks' is used if User-ID is enabled
description: If User-ID is configured, use the Include/Exclude Networks section to limit the User-ID scope to operate only on trusted networks. There is rarely a legitimate need to allow WMI probing or other User identification on an untrusted network.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 2.4 Ensure that 'Include/Exclude Networks' is used if User-ID is enabled

audit.command: Navigate to Device > User Identification > User Mapping > Include/Exclude Networks. Verify that all trusted internal networks have a Discovery value of Include. Verify that all untrusted external networks have a Discovery value of Exclude. Note that any value in the trusted networks list implies that all other networks are untrusted.

remediation.command: Navigate to Device > User Identification > User Mapping > Include/Exclude Networks. Set all trusted internal networks to have a Discovery value of Include. Set all untrusted external networks to have a Discovery value of Exclude. Note that any value in the trusted networks list implies that all other networks are untrusted.

title: Ensure that the User-ID Agent has minimal permissions if User-ID is enabled
description: If the integrated (on-device) User-ID Agent is utilized, the Active Directory account for the agent should only be a member of the Event Log Readers group, Distributed COM Users group, and Domain Users group. If the Windows User-ID agent is utilized, the Active Directory account for the agent should only be a member of the Event Log Readers group, Server Operators group, and Domain Users group.

title: Ensure remote access capabilities for the User-ID service account are forbidden.
description: Restrict the User-ID service account's ability to gain remote access into the organization. audit.command: Auditing is operating-system dependent. In addition, domain administrative accounts should not have remote desktop (RDP) access to all domain member workstations.

For instance, in Windows Active Directory, this account should be removed from any group that grants the account access to VPN or Wireless access. In addition, domain administrative accounts by default have remote desktop (RDP) access to all domain member workstations - this should be explicitly denied for this account.

title: Ensure that URL Filtering uses the action of "block" or "override" on the URL categories
description: Ideally, deciding which URL categories to block, and which to allow, is a joint effort between IT and another entity of authority within an organization—such as the legal department or administration. For most organizations, blocking or requiring an override on the following categories represents a minimum baseline: adult, hacking, command- and-control, copyright-infringement, extremism, malware, phishing, proxy-avoidance- and-anonymizers, and parked. Some organizations may add "unknown" and "dynamic- dns" to this list, at the expense of some support calls on those topics. PASS requires a URL filtering profile with block or override categories; confirm the organisation's designated categories are listed. Audited against the PAN-OS running configuration in set format: run 'set cli config-output-format set', then 'configure' and 'show' (or 'show config running') and save the full output.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 6.9 Ensure that URL Filtering uses the action of "block" or "override" on the URL categories

title: Ensure that a Zone Protection Profile with an enabled SYN Flood Action of SYN Cookies is attached to all untrusted zones
description: Enable the SYN Flood Action of SYN Cookies for all untrusted zones. The Alert, Activate, and Maximum settings for SYN Flood Protection depend highly on the environment and device used. Perform traffic analysis on the specific environment and firewall to determine accurate thresholds. Do not rely on default values to be appropriate for an environment. Setting these values for all interfaces is an approach that should be considered by many organizations, as traffic floods can result from internal testing or malware as well. As a rough ballpark for most environments, an Activate value of 50% of the firewall's maximum "New sessions per second"/CPS is a conservative setting. PASS requires a zone protection profile with tcp-syn syn-cookies and at least one zone using a zone protection profile; confirm every untrusted zone has it. Audited against the PAN-OS running configuration in set format: run 'set cli config-output-format set', then 'configure' and 'show' (or 'show config running') and save the full output.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 6.15 Ensure that a Zone Protection Profile with an enabled SYN Flood Action of SYN Cookies is attached to all untrusted zones

remediation.command:
configure
set network profiles zone-protection-profile ZPP flood tcp-syn enable yes
set network profiles zone-protection-profile ZPP flood tcp-syn syn-cookies alarm-rate 20000 activate-rate 25000 maximal-rate 1000000
set zone <untrust> network zone-protection-profile ZPP

Perform traffic analysis on the specific environment and firewall to determine accurate thresholds. Do not rely on default values to be appropriate for an environment. Less aggressive settings are typically appropriate for trusted zones, such as setting an action of alert for all scan types. Attach appropriate Zone Protection profiles meeting these criteria to all zones. Separate Zone Protection profiles for trusted and untrusted zones is a best practice.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 6.17 Ensure that all zones have Zone Protection Profiles with all Reconnaissance Protection settings enabled, tuned, and set to appropriate actions

audit.command: Network > Network Profiles > Zone Protection > Reconnaissance Protection: TCP Port Scan enabled, action block-ip (track-by source, duration 600), interval 5, threshold 20; Host Sweep enabled, action block, interval 10, threshold 30; UDP Port Scan enabled, action alert, interval 10, threshold 20. Confirm all zones use the profile. CLI: show network profiles zone-protection-profile <name> scan.

remediation.command:
Navigate to Network > Network Profiles > Zone Protection > Zone Protection Profile > Reconnaissance Protection. Set TCP Port Scan to enabled, its Action to block-ip, its Interval to 5, and its Threshold to 20. For block-ip, set the "Track By" is set to source and "Duration" is set to 600 seconds. Set Host Sweep to enabled, its Action to block, its Interval to 10, and its Threshold to
30. Set UDP Port Scan to enabled, its Action to alert, its Interval to 10, and its Threshold to 20.

title: Ensure all zones have Zone Protection Profiles that drop specially crafted packets
description: For all zones, attach a Zone Protection Profile that is configured to drop packets with a spoofed IP address or a mismatched overlapping TCP segment, and packets with malformed, strict source routing, or loose source routing IP options set.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 6.18 Ensure all zones have Zone Protection Profiles that drop specially crafted packets

audit.command: Network > Network Profiles > Zone Protection > Packet Based Attack Protection: confirm Spoofed IP address, Mismatched overlapping TCP segment, Strict Source Routing, Loose Source Routing and Malformed are checked (set ... discard-ip-spoof yes, discard-overlapping-tcp-segment-mismatch yes, discard-strict-source-routing yes, discard-loose-source-routing yes, discard-malformed-option yes) and that all zones use the profile.

set network profiles zone-protection-profile ZPP discard-overlapping-tcp-segment-mismatch yes
set network profiles zone-protection-profile ZPP discard-strict-source-routing yes

# CIS guidance:

title: Ensure that User Credential Submission uses the action of "block" or "continue" on the URL categories
description: Ideally user names and passwords user within an organization are not used with third party sites. Some sanctioned SAS applications may have connections to the corporate domain, in which case they will need to be exempt from the user credential submission policy through a custom URL category.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 6.19 Ensure that User Credential Submission uses the action of "block" or "continue" on the URL categories

audit.command: Navigate to Objects > Security Profiles > URL Filtering. Choose the Categories tab. Verify that the User Credential Submitting action on all enabled URL categories is set to either block or continue. Under the User Credential Detection tab ensure the User Credential Detection is set to a value appropriate to your organization, and is not set to Disabled. Verify that the Log Severity value is set to a value appropriate to your organization and your logging or SIEM solution.

remediation.command: Navigate to Objects > Security Profiles > URL Filtering. Choose the Categories tab. Set the User Credential Submitting action on all enabled URL categories is either block or continue, as appropriate to your organization and the category. Under the User Credential Detection tab set the User Credential Detection value to a setting appropriate to your organization, any value except Disabled. Set the Log Severity to a value appropriate to your organization and your logging or SIEM solution.

title: Ensure application security policies exist when allowing traffic from an untrusted zone to a more trusted zone
description: When permitting traffic from an untrusted zone, such as the Internet or guest network, to a more trusted zone, such as a DMZ segment, create security policies specifying which specific applications are allowed. **Enhanced Security Recommendation: ** Require specific application policies when allowing any traffic, regardless of the trust level of a zone. Do not rely solely on port permissions. This may require SSL interception, and may also not be possible in all environments.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall 11 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 7.1 Ensure application security policies exist when allowing traffic from an untrusted zone to a more trusted zone

audit.command: Navigate to Policies > Security. For all Security Policies that transit from a less trusted to a more trusted interface, that the appropriate Application and Service values are set. For instance, for a web server exposed to the internet from a DMZ: Source tab: Zone set to OUTSIDE / Address set to Any Destination tab: Zone set to DMZ / Address set to [DMZ Host Object] Application tab: set to web-browsing Service/URL Category tab: set Service to ether: application-default or: service-http and/or service-https **Enhanced Security Recommendation: ** Assess this setting ... (Full steps: CIS 7.1.)

remediation.command:
Navigate to Policies > Security. For all Security Policies that transit from a less trusted to a more trusted interface, set the Application and Service values to match the exposed application. For instance, for a web server exposed to the internet from a DMZ: Source tab: Zone set to OUTSIDE / Address set to Any Destination tab: Zone set to DMZ / Address set to [DMZ Host Object] Application tab: set to web-browsing Service/URL Category tab:
set Service to ether:
application-default or:
service-http and/or service-https
**Enhanced Security Recommendation: ** Set these values for Policies on all Interfaces, for traffic in all directions. For each Security Policy, set the Application and Service values to match the exposed application.

title: Ensure NTP servers use authentication
description: Unauthenticated NTP can be spoofed to shift the clock and invalidate logs and certificates. PASS requires a primary or secondary NTP server with authentication-type symmetric-key or autokey. Audited against the PAN-OS running configuration in set format: run 'set cli config-output-format set' then 'show config running' (or 'show' in configure mode) and save the output.
reference: CIS Palo Alto Firewall Benchmark - Device Setup - NTP servers (verify section number for your PAN-OS release)

remediation.command:
configure
set deviceconfig system ntp-servers primary-ntp-server ntp-server-address <ntp1>
set deviceconfig system ntp-servers primary-ntp-server authentication-type symmetric-key key-id 1 algorithm sha1 authentication-key <key>
repeat for secondary-ntp-server
